item.title: About
item.description:
Visit the W6YL Station

The W6YL station, often called the “shack,” is located in Engineering 376A, in the back-right corner of the IEEE club room.

We do not currently have regular station open hours. If you would like to visit, contact us on Discord or email arc@w6yl.org.

Club Meetings

W6YL meets every Tuesday from 4:30–5:30 p.m. during the Fall 2026 semester.

Meetings are held at the W6YL station in Engineering 376A. We discuss club activities, work on projects and give new and prospective members an opportunity to explore the station and learn about amateur radio.

item.title: Nets
item.description:
Tuesday W6YL UHF Net

W6YL holds an amateur radio net every Tuesday at 7 p.m. on the W6YL repeater.

A radio net is a scheduled on-air gathering where amateur radio operators check in and communicate as a group.

Club members and other licensed amateur radio operators are welcome to check in.

New to amateur radio? Come to a club meeting and we can show you how a net works.

item.title: QSL Info
item.description:
QSL Information

QSL cards are used by amateur radio operators to confirm radio contacts.

Mailing Address

Please address QSL cards to:

W6YL — SJSU Amateur Radio Club
Electrical Engineering Department
One Washington Square
San José, CA 95192-0084
USA

QSL Policy

We will try to send a QSL card for contacts when club resources permit.

We generally do not send QSL cards for FT8 contacts unless one is requested.

item.title: Repeaters
item.description:
Repeaters

W6YL SJSU Repeater (UHF)

Open to public, great coverage troughout the campus and surrounding areas.
Located on top of Engineering building.
Frequency: 443.900
Tone: 100.00 Hz
Offset: +5.000 MHz

Our repeater has PL reverse burst enabled, so you can set a recieve tone of 100.0 Hz and have no squelch burst at the end :D

MDC1200

Some members use MDC1200 data on this repeater for paging, so you may hear periodic data bursts.
Please do not enable PTT ID as this is percieved as annoying to radios with no MDC mute.

Awards and Club History

W6YL has a long history of participating in amateur radio contests and activities. The club’s archives include certificates and awards from previous generations of SJSU amateur radio operators.

Selected Awards

ARRL 10-Meter Contest — 1977

ARRL Sweepstakes CW — 1997

ARRL Sweepstakes Phone — 1997

item.title: Getting Started
item.description:
New to Amateur Radio?

You do not need a license or previous radio experience to join W6YL.

Amateur radio — often called ham radio — is a hobby and technical service that lets licensed operators communicate by radio while learning about electronics, antennas, radio propagation and communications technology.

Your First Visit

Come to one of our Tuesday meetings from 4:30–5:30 p.m. in Engineering 376A.

Club members can show you the station, explain the equipment and help you figure out what part of amateur radio interests you.

item.title: Projects and Activities
item.description:
Projects and Activities

W6YL gives students opportunities to learn amateur radio through hands-on projects and on-air activities.

Activities may include:

  • Operating the W6YL amateur radio station
  • Antenna projects and testing
  • Radio programming and configuration
  • Amateur radio contests
  • Weekly radio nets
  • Licensing and operating practice
  • Digital communications
  • Station and repeater maintenance

Current Projects

Check back for updates on current club projects, or join us at a Tuesday meeting to get involved.
